title: ATR boots without OPTION: boot_entry enters start, start's path unmaps the BASIC ROM

defect.symptom: the free ATR only reached the game when the player held OPTION at power-on
defect.cause: boot_entry ended in rts and relied on OS coldstart jumping through DOSVEC. Coldstart only does that when no cartridge is enabled; with BASIC enabled it starts BASIC instead.
defect.prior_measurement: feasibility session, trace emulator: with BASIC enabled the ATR loads all 182 sectors and PC then lands at $A8AA inside the BASIC ROM at frame 223; the menu never arrives by frame 2500. With BASIC off the menu arrives at frame 555.
defect.why_it_was_unnoticed: all four boot-smoke cold sessions ran the emulator with -nobasic, so no gate ever exercised the OS path that fails.

before: boot_entry: jsr boot_stage2_atr_entry; nop; MEMLO/APPMHI = $3B00; DOSVEC lo = <start; clc; boot_return: rts
OS coldstart resumes and jumps through DOSVEC only if no cartridge is enabled
after: boot_stage2_atr_entry: jsr disable_basic_rom, then the manifest validation and the SIO chunk load as before
boot_entry: jsr boot_stage2_atr_entry; MEMLO/APPMHI = $3B00; DOSVEC lo = <start; jmp start
the OS is never returned to; boot_return is an rts the OS JSRs once as the init vector, and now shares the rts of disable_basic_rom
boot_stage2_xex_entry: jsr disable_basic_rom, then boot_chunk_ready = $02; jmp start (unchanged otherwise)
boot_sequence_change.disable_basic_rom: lda PORTB / ora #$02 / sta PORTB / lda #$01 / sta BASICF / rts
boot_sequence_change.portb_contract: read-modify-write, so bit 0 (OS ROM enable), bit 7 (self-test disable) and the bank-select bits are all preserved; only bit 1 is forced to 1
boot_sequence_change.warm_start: BASICF ($03F8) = $01 is the OS flag the warm start re-reads to set PORTB bit 1, so RESET does not map the ROM back in
boot_sequence_change.dosvec: still published (lo in boot_entry, hi in boot_stage2_atr_entry) for the warm-start path and for the boot-smoke ATR entry-identity invariant

ordering.question: writes into a mapped ROM window are lost, so when is the window unmapped?
ordering.chosen: at each medium's stage-2 entry, i.e. before the ATR's SIO chunk load and before the XEX's jmp start - strictly earlier than every write either medium makes
ordering.why: nothing in this build targets $A000-$BFFF today (the ATR chunk staging buffer is $8100 and no segment in cfg/atari-boot.cfg loads above $9FFF), so no write was being lost before the change either. Unmapping first makes that structural instead of incidental: the window is RAM for the whole runtime and a later change cannot silently lose a write into it.
ordering.why_not_start: start would be the single natural site, but the fixed $01A3 resident bootstrap prefix has fewer than three bytes free and could not hold even the jsr. Both stage-2 entries are outside that prefix and both run before start.
ordering.why_not_boot_entry: boot_entry must stay exactly 24 bytes: start is pinned at $201E because scripts/build.mjs requires resident_runtime_suffix at $21C1 = start + $01A3, which is also BOOT_STAGE2's reviewed run address.

placement.routine_location: the 14 B of retired 4.5M-M3 padding (the removed hybrid_c_heavy_publish copy) inside the bootstrap prefix; the routine is exactly 14 B including the rts, so hostile_weapon_step_masks and every later address are unchanged
placement.note: the initial block was exactly full, so any byte of boot-path code costs a sector. Deliberate growth under owner decision 22; docs/boot-deadline-baseline.json was NOT re-recorded because the measured ATR menu frame did not move.

boot_smoke.emulator: Atari800 7.1.2 PAL/XL, instrumented observer, 0 guest bytes
boot_smoke.added: the BASIC-enabled half of the matrix: -basic instead of -nobasic, both media, both cold RAM fills
observations: the ATR menu frame did not move on the BASIC-off sessions despite the extra transport sector (554, delta 0 against the committed baseline)

with BASIC enabled both media reach the menu EARLIER (XEX 383, ATR 538) - OS coldstart takes a different, shorter path when a cartridge is enabled. Both are far inside the 3,000-frame ceiling and inside the +10 warn band measured downward.

negative_control.method: the pre-fix src/main.s was rebuilt and run against the new eight-session gate
negative_control.result: atr-a5-basic FAILS ("did not reach a complete loader raster by frame 300"); the four -nobasic sessions and both xex-*-basic sessions pass
negative_control.conclusion: the new coverage reproduces exactly the reported defect and localises it to ATR x BASIC-enabled. The XEX was never affected: it enters at RUNAD = boot_stage2_xex_entry and never executes boot_entry, so it never depended on DOSVEC.

test_suite.method: full node --test tests/*.test.mjs, A/B against HEAD 80bf1e2 on the same machine
test_suite.note: the 112 failures are the pre-existing set caused by the stale, currently un-regenerable docs/runtime-wall-trace.json; see runtime-wall-trace-report-regeneration-blocked.md. npm test itself is blocked at HEAD too - it runs a final build, which refuses to bind to that stale report.
pins_re_recorded: tests/starfield.test.mjs: manifest.transportCapacity.initialBootSectors 103 -> 104, deliberate, with the reason in place

tests/runtime-wall-trace.test.mjs: the boot-smoke session list is now asserted as a (medium, cold RAM fill) matrix per BASIC state instead of a pinned count of 4, so it validates both the stale committed 4-session report and a live 8-session one exactly

documentation.docs/hardware-testing.md: the "No BASIC dependency" line was WRONG before this fix and is RIGHT after it; the correction is recorded inline, with two new cold-start boxes and a real-hardware box
documentation.docs/memory-map.md: $A000-$BFFF is now unconditionally RAM from disable_basic_rom onward, not a window whose contents depended on how the player started the machine
documentation.docs/architecture.md: cold startup section records the new handoff and the 104-sector initial block

not_proven: real hardware. This changes the boot contract and no session can run a 65XE. The ATR must be booted from SIO2SD on a machine with BASIC enabled, nothing held on the keyboard, and again with OPTION held; and RESET during gameplay must not bring the ROM back. Emulator success is necessary but not sufficient.

pal_timing_audit.procedure: default runtime-wall-trace run, then --raider-formation-only, --raider-sector-only, --debris-gate-only, --raider-remnant-only, then the standalone summary over build/runtime-wall-trace
pal_timing_audit.note: 1,464 cycles on raider-remnant-rapid-xex-hard frame 1945 is byte-for-byte the Option D worst margin: this change adds no gameplay-time work, only 14 B of one-shot boot code and 6 B of call sites.
pal_timing_audit.replay_set_named: the default wall-trace set (64 replays, including the eleven baseline-9040 sessions, targeted, parallax cadence, fighter flash, debris effects, weapon pickup and its traversal/contact/overlap sessions, the three director-completion runs, early-enemy, memory-integrity, lower-playfield, engine startup and engine-restart) plus two-pmg-raiders-xex-hard, raider-sector-xex-hard, the three debris-gate replays and the three raider-remnant replays
